items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: Jazz at the Philharmonic came over with Oscar Peterson and Ray Brown, Ella Fitzgerald. At that particular time... This is where we all congregated after we got off of work.

ctx.x: The unique experience playing in Paris was that Sarah Vaughan went on stage, she was the only one on stage, I mean visible to the audience. The band played behind the curtain, including me. So, to actually communicate with her the way I had been proved a little problem to begin with, but we finally got cues together and things turned out all right. But it seems as if we were there at least three or four weeks, I believe.

During that particular time, Jazz at the Philharmonic came over with Oscar Peterson and Ray Brown, Ella Fitzgerald. At that particular time, the boxer, Sugar Ray Robinson, had a club over there. This is where we all congregated after we got off of work. It turned out to be a very happy time.

After finishing that engagement at this club... Someone had opened a club over there, and they gave the club a name... As a matter of fact, they named the club after Sarah. The club was called the Chez Sassy, I think. I thought that was a rather unique thing, because we'd only been in Paris a short while, and all of a sudden there's a club there with Sarah's name. Anyway, I don't remember how long we played there, but
